title: Best Period and Ovulation Tracker Apps for Nigerians
description: Compare four period and ovulation trackers for Nigerian women trying to conceive. See sign-up, reminders, prices and where each app keeps your dates.
share: If you are choosing a period or ovulation tracker in Nigeria, this comparison shows what four apps let you do, what they cost and where they keep your dates.
h1: Best period and ovulation tracker apps in Nigeria
crumb: Best period and ovulation tracker apps in Nigeria
kicker: For Nigerian women choosing a tracker while trying to conceive
answer: If you want to start without signing up and print questions for the clinic, choose Wholesome Girlies. If you want daily symptoms and reminders, Flo or Period Calendar gives you more. Clue suits you if you want its expert-written guides. No calendar app can tell you the exact day you ovulate from dates alone. Flo ranks 1 and Period Calendar ranks 2 in the Nigerian App Store Health and Fitness chart.

apps.name: Wholesome Girlies
apps.best: A woman trying to conceive who wants no account and a plan.
apps.body: The Period Tracker and Ovulation Calculator open on the date field with no account and no card. Your dates stay on your phone, and after three logged periods the tracker uses your own average. The Trying-to-Conceive Blueprint, the appointment questions and the checklist for your partner sit beside them.
apps.watch: You cannot note symptoms. Reminders go into your own phone calendar when you tap Add to my calendar. The calculator counts 14 days back from your next period, so we make no accuracy claim.

apps.name: Flo
apps.best: You want to note symptoms daily, get reminders and see your entries on another device.
apps.body: Flo lets you note symptoms, sends reminders and shows your entries on your other devices. You can also read many articles. It ranks 1 in the Nigerian App Store Health and Fitness chart. Premium costs nothing on Android in Nigeria for one year under Pass It On.
apps.watch: On iPhone, the lowest Premium price is ₦3,900 (about $3). The highest is ₦29,900 (about $22). Flo writes for women worldwide.

apps.name: Period Calendar
apps.best: A woman who wants reminders and a calendar with years of history.
apps.body: Period Calendar ranks 2 in the Nigerian App Store Health and Fitness chart and first in Nigerian Google Play search for period tracker. Nigerian reviewers praise its notifications and how long they have used it.
apps.watch: Google Play marks it as containing ads, its Pro tier costs ₦69,900 (about $52), and reviews mention ads.

apps.name: Clue
apps.best: You want expert-written guides with your cycle tracker.
apps.body: Clue is a cycle tracker from Berlin, and it says it does not sell data to advertisers. Forecasts need the Plus tier. It runs from ₦1,500 (about $1) to ₦12,900 (about $10) on the Nigerian App Store.
apps.watch: It ranks 46 in the Nigerian chart, and it is not written for Nigeria.

faq.q: Which period tracker app is best in Nigeria?
faq.a: It depends on the job. Flo and Period Calendar rank 1 and 2 in the Nigerian App Store chart and track daily. Wholesome Girlies suits a woman trying to conceive who wants no account, dates on her phone and a plan for the clinic.

faq.q: Which app predicts ovulation most accurately?
faq.a: No app on this page can detect ovulation from dates alone, and we make no accuracy claim. A Journal of Medical Internet Research analysis of 7,043 tracked cycles found ovulation does not sit reliably at the midpoint. Take your last three or four period dates to a clinician.
No. It is educational, not medical advice. See a doctor if you have been trying for a year, or six months if you are over 35.

doctor: See a doctor after twelve months of trying, or six months if you are over 35. See one sooner if your cycles are very irregular, shorter than 21 days or longer than 35, or have stopped. Take your last three or four period dates with you.

disclaimer.strong: This page compares apps. It cannot tell you when you will conceive.
disclaimer.rest: A calendar predicts and does not detect. It is educational, not medical advice, and no clinician has reviewed it yet.
